verdicts.reason: A has a clear left-to-right banner flow: image, then headline and subcopy aligned on one left edge, then the CTA. But the crop shows a green hill, not the original sea and sky. The small white Meridian logo sits on that busy image with weak contrast, and the Book Now button is pushed almost against the right edge. B's oversized logo straddles the image/blue-panel boundary, so 'Meridian' crosses the seam and sits half on the busy photo, which is an unwanted collision. Its subcopy is tiny next to a huge CTA that competes with the headline, and the CTA is crammed toward the bottom-right with an odd sliver of blue beyond it.
